title: Fix the Unchecked Calloc Result
description: The program should allocate a zero-initialized array using calloc and use it.
expectedBehavior: If the allocation fails (as an unreasonably large request like this likely would), the program should detect that and report it instead of crashing.
actualProblem: Requesting an enormous, likely-unsatisfiable amount of memory causes calloc() to return NULL, but that return value is never checked. Writing to arr[0] then dereferences a NULL pointer and crashes.
explanation: Like malloc(), calloc() returns NULL when it cannot satisfy the requested allocation (for example, if the size is unreasonably large). That return value must always be checked before the pointer is used.
